Where one balance is read under two ids, as the HyperEVM unit found for stHYPE and wstHYPE, a rise booked under the rebasing id also removes the yield of pools in the other id, so the answer decides how far the Ethereum finding reaches.

leads.question: Does a distributor that pays holders on a third party's call owe anything to the PoolManager address on any chain? Check the Merkl distributor, Compound style claim functions, and any airdrop contract with a claim for an arbitrary account, for each of the ten largest token holdings of each PoolManager. What does one claim pay, in which token, and is that token the currency of any pool?
leads.why: A claim that any account can trigger raises a token balance of the PoolManager inside the caller's transaction. With sync before and settle after, the caller is credited the whole amount (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 358-364). The PoolManager is among the largest holders of many tokens, so reward programs that pay by holding are likely to list it. The Ethereum unit checked three such triggers on mainnet and none on the other chains.

leads.question: Which tokens held by the PoolManager change state for the sender when the PoolManager sends a transfer of zero: a transfer cooldown per sender, a counter of transfers per block, a reward that is claimed to the sender, or a fee swap inside the token? The call costs nothing: take(token, anyRecipient, 0) inside an unlock.
leads.why: take with amount zero makes the PoolManager call transfer and owes nothing (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, 368-369). A token that limits how often one sender may transfer would let any account use up that limit in every block and so stop every payout of that token to all pools, with no role and no cost beyond gas. The verifier of the established L1 unit asked this for three chains only.

leads.question: Repeat the special address sweep with a forwarding stub placed at the PoolManager address by state override and a different account as transaction sender. For which targets does the answer to empty calldata with value, transfer(address,uint256), balanceOf(address) or a hook selector differ from the answer to a top-level call from the PoolManager address?
leads.why: See the gap entry. The real calls are inner frames (src/types/Currency.sol:48, 73, 94 and src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134). A target that pays or credits the origin, or that accepts only contract callers, was tested in the one shape that cannot occur.

leads.question: Through the Quoter listed in state/networks.json for each chain, quote an exact input and an exact output swap that crosses at least three initialized ticks in the largest pool, in both directions, and compare the amounts with a transcription of src/libraries/Pool.sol, SwapMath.sol and SqrtPriceMath.sol run on the pool state read through extsload at the same block. Do all 21 networks agree to the last unit?
leads.why: This runs the deployed PoolManager bytecode through each node's own execution path, including the compiled path on Monad, the evm2 path on Tempo and the fused interpreter on BNB Smart Chain, which the init code probes do not reach. A network whose result differs by one unit in the swapper's favour would let pools pay out more than they hold.

leads.question: On Tempo a write to an empty slot costs 250,000 gas and one transaction may use 30,000,000. What does one swap step cost when it crosses an initialized tick whose two fee growth slots are written for the first time, how many such crossings fit in one transaction, and what does it cost an ordinary account to initialize that many ticks with dust positions around the price of the largest pool? Does a removal of liquidity ever write an empty slot?
leads.why: The L3 profile has no gas figure. At 500,000 gas for the two fee growth slots alone, about sixty first time crossings fill a transaction, so dust positions can force a large trade into many transactions (src/libraries/Pool.sol swap loop and tick crossing). Removal of liquidity touches two ticks and should stay possible, which the measurement would confirm.

attempts.answer: Measured by simulation at block 50,363,527. A first crossing of a tick with both fee growth outside slots empty costs 504,684 gas, with one slot empty about 254,500 gas. 58 such crossings fit in the 30,000,000 gas of one transaction. A dust position on a fresh tick costs about 540,000 gas, which is 0.0003 USD at the base fee floor. A removal of liquidity can write two empty slots, the fee growth inside values of the position, about 500,000 gas, and never crosses ticks, so it stays possible. Filed as a low finding with effect degrade.

leads.question: Do transactions that call the PoolManager on Tempo count against mainBlockGeneralGasLimit, which block 50,314,865 reports as 30,000,000 against a block gasLimit of 500,000,000? Is the base fee of 600,000,000 per gas fixed by the protocol, and does a proposer order transactions inside the general limit by tip or by arrival? What does it cost per day to fill the general limit of every block with cheap transactions?
leads.why: At the base fee seen in 1,024 consecutive blocks, 30,000,000 gas costs 0.018 dollars per block, and blocks arrive about every 0.54 seconds, which is under 3,000 dollars per day if the fee does not rise with use. Every exit from the PoolManager is a call to unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114) and would compete for that limit. If ordering is by arrival, or the fee is fixed, an ordinary account could hold liquidity providers out for as long as it pays. The stablecoin unit did not look at fee dynamics.

attempts.answer: PoolManager transactions count against the general limit: the payload builder defers a transaction that is not a payment once 30,000,000 general gas is used. The base fee is no longer fixed. Since T7 it follows the EIP-1559 formula against a 10,000,000 gas target between 600,000,000 and 12,000,000,000 attodollars, so the 600,000,000 seen in 1,024 blocks is the floor of a quiet chain. Ordering is by tip. Filling the general lane costs 0.018 USD per block at the floor and 0.36 USD at the cap, about 57,600 USD per day at the cap, and a withdrawal that outbids the filler's tip is included first.

leads.question: Does the execution client of each of these OP Stack chains contain a rule that turns a user deposit into a failed deposit or leaves it out, as intercept_blacklisted_deposit does in the X Layer client? Search the handler and block executor of base/node, world-chain, celo-kona, mega-evm and the Conduit builds for calls made before a deposit executes.
leads.why: Forced inclusion through the L1 portal is the mitigation that every operator filtering finding on these chains relies on (F-017, F-030). On X Layer it turned out to be voidable at the execution layer. Soneium already restricts listed contracts at its RPC and sequencer and nobody read its execution client for the same rule.

attempts.answer: MegaETH part. mega-evm has no rule that fails or drops a deposit because of its sender or target. before_run handles only transactions from the system address, and the block executor sends deposits through the general limiter with an exemption from the data availability tests. A deposit fails only on resource limits that apply to its own execution. The closed mega-reth payload builder was not read. The other chains of this lead belong to other units.

leads.question: Do the B20 precompile on Base, the CAS20 dispatcher in the Jenner client and the Robinhood stock tokens have any path on which transfer returns true while the amount is credited to an account other than the named recipient or held by a guard contract, as TIP-20 does on Tempo for a recipient whose receive policy rejects the sender? Who names the account that can recover such funds?
leads.why: F-033 shows that on Tempo a payout can succeed for the PoolManager and never reach the recipient (src/types/Currency.sol:60-75 accepts a true word). OUSD exists on Base and on Tempo under the same policy administrator. If a recipient side policy on another chain can be set by a third party for a router or a wallet, payouts to it are diverted with no failed call to warn the user.

leads.question: Settle the two plausible HyperEVM items with one fact: when a treasury deployer names an EVM address as AQAv2 treasury, must that address sign a message, send a CoreWriter action or hold a HyperCore account first? Read the HyperCore action schema for the designation and look for a designation whose treasury address is a contract.
leads.why: F-020 and the new AQAv2 finding stay plausible on this point alone. If no consent is required, unsigned system transfers can move an ERC-20 balance out of a contract that never called transfer, which breaks assumption A2 for the PoolManager and changes the actor from operator to whoever can pass the stake and vote conditions.

attempts.answer: Same fact as L-180: no signature, CoreWriter action or HyperCore account of the named address preceded the system transfers. The node also sends transfers in the name of the CoreDepositWallet, a contract, so a contract address can be the sender of a system transaction. I found no second AQAv2 token, so there is no example of a designation whose treasury address is a contract. The actor stays operator, because activation needs a validator vote and two deployers with 500,000 HYPE staked each.

leads.question: Settle F-024 with one fact: is the risk control filter of the block builder switched on for the X Layer mainnet sequencer, and has any source hash been written to the deposit blacklist at 0x59055c0ef0be92018b33f877a3eB816355791727? An indexer with full log access for that contract answers the second part.
leads.why: F-024 is plausible because the filter state on mainnet is unknown, and the new high finding on voided deposits rests on source at one tag. Both verdicts depend on whether the rules are in use.

leads.question: Without comparing code, does the Unichain predeploy behave as src/PoolManager.sol says? With a caller contract placed by state override, check by eth_call: settle with value after sync of a token reverts with NonzeroNativeValue, settle after sync(address(0)) credits msg.value, a settle without payment credits zero, take reverts while locked, clear accepts only the exact positive delta, mint and burn move the delta and the claim by the same amount, and collectProtocolFees for a synced token reverts.
leads.why: Every Unichain clearance assumes src/ describes a contract of a different size that was placed at genesis. A behaviour test is the method the owner has not ruled out. A missing native value guard there would matter less than on Celo because ETH has no ERC-20 face on Unichain, yet the other checks cover the accounting of every pool on that chain.

leads.question: On Celo and Arc, read the deployed Universal Router and PositionManager: do they call sync(address(0)) before every native settle, do they ever treat the CELO token or 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 as the wrapped native currency, and what do they do with a route that names both address(0) and the token face of the same balance?
leads.why: The two chains are the only ones where the native asset has a transferable ERC-20 face, so they are where the guard at src/PoolManager.sol:356 and the comment at line 348 matter. The settlement model cleared core. The periphery that ordinary users go through was not read on either chain, and a router that settles the face with msg.value or skips the sync leaves its users with reverts or with funds credited to nobody.

attempts.answer: Arc half answered and safe, Celo half not examined by this unit. On Arc the Universal Router, Universal Router 2.1.2 and PositionManager sync address(0) before every native settle that the SETTLE action makes, never treat 0x3600 as wrapped native (their WETH9 immutable is a contract that reverts on every call), and handle a route that names both ids as two currencies. Paying the wrong id ends in CurrencyNotSettled.

First question answered for both networks: the deployed Universal Routers and PositionManagers on Celo and Arc call sync(address(0)) before every native settle (verified source for the 2.1.x routers, code match for the others). The questions about the wrapped native setting and about routes that name both faces were not examined in this unit.

leads.question: The Elysium bridge contract on HyperEVM holds 298,480 HYPE and executes child chain messages as calls made by itself. What happens when an Elysium account sends a message whose target is the HYPE bridge address 0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222, a token system address or CoreWriter: is a HyperCore balance credited to the bridge contract, and can a later message spend it?
leads.why: The arbitrum-family unit left this open. The backing of every bridged asset on Elysium, including the HYPE and USDC that its PoolManager holds, sits in that contract. An ordinary Elysium account that can move the backing into a HyperCore account leaves holders of the bridged tokens, pools included, unable to withdraw to HyperEVM.

attempts.answer: A simulated executeCall from the Elysium outbox shows that the Bridge sends HYPE to 0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222 and calls CoreWriter without restriction, and both name the Bridge itself as the HyperCore user. A later message could spend that HyperCore account. The escrowed 297,189 HYPE is not reachable this way, because the Bridge sends only the value of a message and that value was burned on Elysium. No such message has been executed and the Bridge has no HyperCore account. The gateway that holds bridged tokens was not read in this cycle.

leads.question: Which go-ethereum commit do the sequencers of the three Nitro chains run (the endpoint reports nitro v3.13.0-rc.9 while the source was read at v3.11.3), and does EVM.Call in that commit keep the balance check for every caller, as the critic saw in OffchainLabs/go-ethereum master, where isSystemCall is used for witness gas only?
leads.why: The source reading of this unit is two releases behind the running build. Upstream go-ethereum now skips the value transfer for the system caller, and a merge of that change into Nitro would need a second look at which ArbOS paths use that caller.

leads.question: Is collect on the Arc fee controller (3,480 bytes at 0x2f2bd3f43880b9644211f16d861b0672aab23782) open to any caller, where does it send native USDC, and can the destination pay it back to the PoolManager inside the same transaction?
leads.why: collectProtocolFees exempts address(0) from the synced currency test with the remark that native settle uses msg.value (src/ProtocolFees.sol:49-52). On Arc and Celo the native balance is also what balanceOf of the token face reports, so a native collection moves the figure that a pending settle of the face will read. The settlement model allowed a withdrawal at any point and found no gain. It did not model a destination that returns the funds.

leads.question: Where is the opcode fusion code of pull request 3395 in the BNB Smart Chain client that validators run, which opcode sequences does it fuse, and which sequences caused the bad block fixed by pull requests 3582 and 3584?
leads.why: The established L1 unit could not find the feature in the five files it read. An interpreter that rewrites bytecode has already produced one consensus fault on this chain, and the PoolManager bytecode is optimizer output with long stack sequences.

leads.question: After T14 activates on 2026-12-08, what does 0xAACC000000000000000000000000000000000000 answer to the PoolManager call shapes, and can an account of the new configurable type be the sender of a transaction whose address was fixed before its code or configuration existed?
leads.why: The address is codeless today and returns success to every call. Assumption A7 and the hook address rule depend on code at an address staying what it was, and a new account type is a new way for behaviour at a fixed address to change.

leads.question: From Blockscout or another indexer, what are the twenty largest token balances of the PoolManager on Soneium, Ink, Zora and World Chain, and which of them rebase, answer at a second address, or have a block list or pause role?
leads.why: The four chains have no L3 record of their own. The issuer finding F-028 lists three of them by analogy.

leads.question: In the parallel executors of Bor (BlockSTM), World Chain (flashblocks validation with block access lists) and Monad (optimistic execution with retries), is a transaction that is re-executed after a conflict always started with an empty transient map, and is the transient map of a discarded attempt ever merged into the state the next transaction reads?
leads.why: Three units cleared A1 from the serial path or from the per transaction state object and each noted that the merge step was not read to the end. The synced currency and reserves are the only PoolManager state that can outlive a call (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:21-32), and a stale pair from a discarded attempt would be read by settle as real.

leads.question: Who controls the hooks that most new pools use, 0x4e3468951d49f2eea976ed0d6e75ffcb44a9a544 and 0x2c668601193e4a081dd82604785e436aff6a2acc on Robinhood Chain and 0x6b1216a40b65c83e9c9e18a562c446697b8cf8ec on Elysium, and what can the owner of each change after pools exist: fees taken through the swap return deltas, a pause, or the code behind the address.
leads.why: A third of the sampled pools on Robinhood Chain and four fifths on Elysium share one hook. The Robinhood hook carries the afterRemoveLiquidity flag, so F-004 applies to every one of its pools at once. The Elysium hook has an owner and takes swap deltas. This is a pool-creator matter, and it decides how much of the liquidity on these chains sits behind a single contract.

leads.question: Which contracts carry the 26 activated Stylus code hashes on Robinhood Chain, and is any of them, or a copy, the hook or a currency of an initialized pool.
leads.why: F-003 now lists Robinhood Chain. Its impact there depends on whether any pool uses a Stylus program. The Initialize logs and the program addresses in the ProgramActivated logs can be joined by an indexer.

leads.question: What does the unpublished build v3.13.0-rc.9 at commit b72783f change against v3.12.4 in the sequencer side filters and in RPC behaviour.
leads.why: The consensus rules are fixed by the consensus-v61 module root, so execution results cannot differ. Sequencer policy can. On Robinhood Chain the address filter and its neighbour effects decide which transactions are accepted, and this cycle could read them only at v3.12.4.

leads.question: When an ArbOS version with Amsterdam rules is scheduled, which transaction types can have the system address 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe as sender or caller, and does evm.Call then let its frames carry value without a balance debit.
leads.why: The fork already contains the branch that skips the balance check and the transfer for that caller and holds it back until Amsterdam. On Nitro chains the sender of an unsigned parent chain message is the parent chain sender plus a fixed offset, so the system address corresponds to parent chain address 0xeeeeffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffeeed. Nobody is known to control it, and a sender without code cannot receive the unlock callback, so I see no path today. The question should be asked again when the version is scheduled.

leads.question: Can a HyperCore spot deployer link a token to the Elysium Bridge, an Elysium gateway or the Outbox on HyperEVM by making that contract send the finalize EVM contract action through CoreWriter, and what do HyperCore system transactions then call on it.
leads.why: Any Elysium account can make the Bridge call CoreWriter with data of its choice. This cycle reasoned that a linked Bridge neither answers transfer nor emits Transfer events and did not test it. The Bridge holds the HYPE that backs the PoolManager's native balance on Elysium.

leads.question: Does the compiled PoolManager, driven through the test routers of src/test on a local chain, give the same deltas, events and revert data as the Python transcription on the cases this unit replayed, in particular the 20,000 hook delta runs of test/CustomAccounting.t.sol:160-266 and the 8,920 cases of the differential against test/bin/v3Factory.bytecode?
leads.why: The transcription follows the source text of PoolManager.sol and Hooks.sol. It cannot show a difference introduced by the compiler, by the via_ir optimiser or by the assembly that copies and parses hook return data, and those parts decide which account is debited. Lead L-024 asks the same for the math libraries only. The check needs forge and nothing outside this repository.

leads.question: Does a build of src/ with the settings in foundry.toml (solc 0.8.26, via_ir, 44444444 optimizer runs, cancun, bytecode_hash none) give a PoolManager runtime of 24009 bytes and the creation code hash 19281018184167079101887460999643277467915809731640262058315305465805214934776 recorded in snapshots/PoolManagerTest.json, and does forge test --isolate reproduce the gas values in snapshots/ without a diff?
leads.why: The creation code hash is the one witness inside the repository that covers every line of src/ at once. A different hash would show that the source text changed after the snapshots were written, and the gas diff would point at the function. This unit could only check the snapshots for plausibility because forge and solc are not installed and nothing may be installed. The check uses only files of this repository.

leads.question: Does test_fuzz_swap in test/libraries/Pool.t.sol pass under the fixed fuzz seed 0x4444 with 1000 runs, or does it reach a zero amountSpecified with a 100 percent swap fee, where line 129 expects InvalidFeeForExactOut and Pool.sol:311-320 returns without a revert?
leads.why: If the committed test fails against the committed source, one of the two was edited after the other, and the comparison operator at Pool.sol:313 would be the place to look. The zero amount path itself changes no state, so the question is about the history of the file and has no direct fund effect.

leads.question: Do several thousand mined Swap, ModifyLiquidity and Donate events per network reproduce from the pool state at the block before, when replayed with a transcription of src/libraries/Pool.sol fed through extsload, including swaps that cross many initialized ticks?
leads.why: This verifier reproduced 107 mined swaps on 20 networks and 370 Quoter quotes on 21 networks with no difference, six mined swaps per network or fewer. HyperEVM returned no PoolManager log in the scanned range and has no mined sample. Monad compiles hot bytecode, BNB Smart Chain has an opcode fusion interpreter, Tempo pins a JIT crate and the Arc release in use is unknown, so a larger sample of mined results on these chains would close the cycle 2 critic gap on execution paths that an eth_call may not take. The method is read only and needs no contract.

leads.question: While the PoolManager is on the G$ block list, does a Superfluid distribution or stream to it raise balanceOf(PoolManager) so that sync and settle credit the payer, and does GoodDollar plan to use adminBurn on the PoolManager's 550,022,104 G$?
leads.why: A credit through agreements would let G$ be sold into the frozen pools while liquidity providers cannot withdraw G$. A burn would leave G$ pool liquidity and G$ claims without backing. The first part needs a simulation with an unlock caller, which this unit did not build.

leads.question: Which contracts are allowedWrappers of the permissioned wrapper tokens on X Layer, and can a user of one of them call wrapToPoolManager for an amount that is covered by underlying tokens already sitting in the wrapper instead of tokens the user paid?
leads.why: A take that names the wrapper as recipient burns wrapper tokens and leaves the underlying in the wrapper. If an allowed router mints against that surplus for the next user, the wrapper supply in the PoolManager can be refilled without payment. The pools are small today (2,000 to 4,000 USD each).

leads.question: What do the values returned by globalTransferSettings() on USDG (1771954688, 86400, 0, 0) limit, and can the issuer use them to cap transfers out of one address per day?
leads.why: A transfer cap on the PoolManager address would make takes of USDG revert once the cap is used, which blocks withdrawals from the 879,000 USD USDG/USDT0 pool without a freeze entry.

leads.question: Which execution client produces Celo mainnet blocks, and do celo-org/op-geth and celo-kona agree on whether transient storage written by debitGasFees is still present in the main call? In op-geth Prepare runs before the debit and nothing clears afterwards, and celo-kona clears after the debit.
leads.why: The two clients would disagree for a fee currency that leaves a transient value behind. The PoolManager is not a fee currency and no registered fee currency is known to call it, so the reach to pool funds is small. The clearance of assumption A1 on Celo should rest on the client that builds blocks.

leads.question: Can a G$ position held through the Celo PositionManager be reduced so that the paired currency leaves while the G$ delta is moved into another position in the same unlock, and how much of the paired currencies do the G$ pools hold?
leads.why: The PositionManager code has no call to PoolManager.mint, so the G$ side of a removal cannot become a claim. If the delta cannot be moved into another position either, a liquidity provider must forfeit the G$ with clear to withdraw the paired currency while the issuer block lasts. This sizes the frozen value of finding 0 and does not change its actor.

leads.question: On an archive node, compare the balance of 0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222 and of the recipient before and after a block that holds a HYPE system transaction, and read what the node does when the recipient reverts.
leads.why: The validator node is closed source. The public clients debit the bridge address, and an observed state diff would confirm that no HYPE is created on the EVM side without a HyperCore debit. The public RPC serves latest state for old blocks, so this needs an archive endpoint.

attempts.answer: Done on two archive endpoints. In four blocks with one HYPE system transfer each, the bridge address lost exactly the transferred value and the recipient gained it, so no HYPE is created on the EVM side. The second half of the lead is open: all 46 observed transfers went to accounts without code, so the node's behaviour for a reverting recipient was not seen. A simulated transfer of this shape to the PoolManager reverts.

leads.question: After the Jenner fork on 2026-12-08, does any new system call or transaction type on BNB Smart Chain run user-chosen code with caller 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe and nonzero value, and does the probe from this unit still return the same words?
leads.why: The client reports a value that nobody paid for that caller. The PoolManager credits msg.value without reading a balance (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354), so one reachable frame of that kind would expose every BNB pool.

leads.question: Which go-ethereum, op-geth and Celo releases contain the system caller rule, and does any sequencer or validator of these chains run one of them as its execution client?
leads.why: The rule is in the source of three clients and was observed on one endpoint only. The public endpoints of the OP Stack chains run op-reth and the Celo endpoint runs an older build, so the running behaviour of other nodes is not shown by this unit's probes.

leads.question: Does Monad burn the balance of a contract that executes SELFDESTRUCT with itself as beneficiary when the contract was not created in the same transaction, or is the zero balance seen in the probe an effect of the state override?
leads.why: Ethereum keeps the balance in that case. A burn rule would be an undocumented opcode difference. It does not reach the PoolManager, whose bytecode has no SELFDESTRUCT, and it would matter to hooks or tokens that use the opcode.

leads.question: Does any account in Tempo's genesis or state hold a nonzero native balance at the EVM level?
leads.why: The interpreter moves value normally when a balance exists. The native branch of settle and take is inert only while no account holds one. A funded account that delegates with EIP-7702 could make inner calls with value even though the transaction itself must carry none.

leads.question: forno.celo.org answers from a reth based client (reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb) and from a Geth build (c7ed55b8 of 2026-08-17). Which client produces Celo blocks today, and does the source of the reth based client keep the separate native balance check for the value of a fee currency transaction and the caller restriction of the transfer precompile?
leads.why: The unit read celo-org/op-geth only. Both backends rejected a transfer precompile call from an unpermissioned address and moved value normally in my probes, so no difference is known. The value check for fee currency transactions was read in one client, and a second client family on the same chain can differ in a path that a probe through eth_call does not reach.

leads.question: Which pools and positions hold the 550 million G$ in the Celo PoolManager, and does the deployed PositionManager offer an exit that takes the other currency while the G$ side is minted as a claim or cleared?
leads.why: The G$ side is frozen by the issuer's block. Core allows mint and clear in place of take (src/PoolManager.sol:310-329). If the periphery only offers a take of both currencies, the other currency of those positions is frozen in practice as well.

leads.question: Which pooled tokens on each chain store the PoolManager address or answer poolManager(), POOL_MANAGER() or poolManagerGateEnabled(), and what does each do when the PoolManager is the sender?
leads.why: ELO on Elysium and v4CRCL on X Layer change their transfer rules for the PoolManager. They were found by a failed dust transfer in a sample of 12 tokens per chain. An indexer pass over all pool currencies with these three selectors would list every token of this kind.

leads.question: Does the PoolManager on these chains hold market tokens of lending protocols whose reward claim names the holder (Venus claimVenus(address), Moonwell and other Compound forks), and how much is accrued for it?
leads.why: On Avalanche 14.84 QI is accrued for the PoolManager and the public claim pays it to the PoolManager when the Comptroller is funded, which a caller can book between sync and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364). The same shape may hold larger sums elsewhere. XVS is among the larger holdings on Unichain.

leads.question: With a tracing endpoint, does a zero amount transfer from the PoolManager write any storage outside the token itself for the largest pooled tokens on these eight chains?
leads.why: Their public endpoints refuse eth_simulateV1 and debug_traceCall, so effects on a second token were judged from gas use and from the token's own balance only.

leads.question: Can a Superfluid distribution to the PoolManager, or a public claim made on its behalf for a distribution pool, raise G$.balanceOf(PoolManager) while the address is blocked, and is any such amount pending for it today?
leads.why: The verified SuperGoodDollar source says a blocked account can still be credited by agreements, and the finding states that no increase can occur. A claim that any account can make for the PoolManager would be one more balance rise that sync and settle book to the caller (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364). The credited G$ could not be taken while the block stands, so the expected result is a clearance with a corrected statement.

leads.question: Which mega-evm revision does mega-reth v2.2.3 pin, and does any MegaETH specification after REX6, or any planned transaction type with more than one top-level call, let a KeylessDeploy sandbox start while contract code of the same transaction has already run or will still run?
leads.why: The sandbox starts with an empty transient map and its state changes are merged into the parent (sandbox/execution.rs lines 583 to 650). The depth check at system/intercept.rs line 301 is the only thing that keeps it apart from a PoolManager unlock or sync in progress. If a sandbox could run between two calls of one transaction, a caller could sync a token outside, pay, settle and mint a claim inside, and settle outside for the same tokens (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364, 322-329).

attempts.answer: The public stateless validator pins mega-evm v1.7.3, and the depth test at system/intercept.rs line 301 is identical at that tag and on main. The specification list ends at REX6 and v1.7.3 removed the REX7 draft. The five documented transaction types each have one top-level call. No path was found that starts a sandbox beside other contract code of the same transaction. The dependency line of mega-reth v2.2.3 itself is not public and stays unconfirmed.

leads.question: When the source of nitro v3.13.0-rc.9 (commit b72783f) is published, do arbos/programs/api.go and arbos/block_processor.go still route Stylus calls through evm.Call on the running StateDB and still restore whole transactions in the group rollback?
leads.why: Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain run this release and raw.githubusercontent.com returns 404 for the tag and the commit, so the clearance for Stylus and for the group rollback rests on master and v3.12.0. A change that gave a Stylus call or a filtered redeem its own state object would separate PoolManager deltas from token transfers (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297).

leads.question: After T14 activates on Tempo mainnet, what does a registered configurable account (code 0xef, served by a native shim) return for the IHooks selectors, for balanceOf and for transfer, and can an address with chosen low 14 bits be derived by varying the salt?

leads.question: Does any crate of tempoxyz/tempo at commit 697ea97, or any later release that mainnet adopts, call evm2 State::committed_copy, Evm::call_tx or Evm::transact from inside a precompile, an opcode handler or a transaction handler while a user call is still running?

leads.question: Which celo-kona revision do the Celo mainnet nodes run, and do op-geth c7ed55b8 and celo-reth produce the same result when a listed fee currency or adapter leaves a nonzero transient slot at the end of debitGasFees?

leads.question: For every currency of an initialized pool whose balance at the PoolManager is above dust, does balanceOf(PoolManager) at block B2 minus balanceOf(PoolManager) at block B1 equal the Transfer logs to the PoolManager minus the Transfer logs from it between the two blocks? This check needs no knowledge of the token and covers rebases, reward pushes, fees on transfer, share accounting, system credits and enshrined tokens with one method. A token with a public trigger and a large pooled balance would be an unprivileged loss.

Blocks 32,501,227 to 32,671,826, 86,399 seconds. Tokens that do not reconcile: 1 second address of one ledger (USDC); 1 system log emitter (0xffffffff). Classes and who can move them. Public trigger: sLGNS, sATH, sKLIMA on Polygon, sNVB and sSAC on BNB Smart Chain, USDI on Ethereum; any account can raise the balance inside one transaction, the balance does not fall back, and sync then settle, or take then repay, yields 8.78 sLGNS per epoch and 4,636.71 USDI today. Scheduled multiplier set by the issuer: xStocks tokens on Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Monad and X Layer; SNDKx went up eightfold at a timestamp; no ordinary account can bracket it. Time formula upward: lending receipt tokens on twelve networks and 666, EXPT, EXPT2; no trigger, nothing to capture. Time formula downward, where the last to withdraw are locked: TURING on Ethereum, PYRE and SMK2 on Robinhood Chain, DDL on Arbitrum One. Base, BNB Smart Chain and X Layer were tested for tokens active in the window only. 43 tokens on Robinhood Chain could not be read at old blocks. A token that changes balance less often than once a day passes this test unless the change fell inside the window.

leads.question: Take the hooks 0x4e3468951d49f2eea976ed0d6e75ffcb44a9a544 and 0x2c668601193e4a081dd82604785e436aff6a2acc on Robinhood Chain, 0x6b1216a40b65c83e9c9e18a562c446697b8cf8ec on Elysium and the proxy hook 0x630e9cac0fff557bd3a01daa111ed253c771bcc0 on X Layer. When an ordinary account calls initialize with a PoolKey that names one of them and two currencies of its own, does the call succeed in eth_call? In the hook's code, do the swap, liquidity and donate callbacks compare the pool id or the currencies with a list of the hook's own pools before they write storage, return deltas, or take, settle or mint for the hook?
leads.why: initialize accepts any address with valid flag bits and records nothing about who may use it (src/PoolManager.sol:117-142, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-127). Each later hook call comes from the PoolManager with a PoolKey and hookData chosen by the caller (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:178-335), and a hook delta is booked to the hook address (src/PoolManager.sol:181, 224). A hook that trusts msg.sender alone can be driven through a pool of worthless tokens, and what it holds or decides for its real pools is then within reach of any account. The victims use a hook the attacker did not write, so the actor would be unprivileged. Earlier sweeps aimed the hook call shape at system addresses only. On Elysium four of five sampled pools use one hook.

leads.question: Which pooled tokens on these chains limit what one address may send or hold over a period: a transfer volume per day or per block, a count of transfers, a cooldown, a maximum balance per holder or an issuer velocity rule? Check the stock tokens and USDG, the Securitize wrappers and multiplier tokens on X Layer, the wrapped stock tokens on Monad and Ink, SPCXB, the B20 and TIP-403 policies, and wBRL and wARS. For each one that does, does a take of the PoolManager's balance that is paid back in the same unlock count against the limit of the PoolManager address?
leads.why: take sends any amount the PoolManager holds before anything is paid in, and the borrower can return it in the same transaction at no cost (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, 104-114). All pools of a token share one sender address. If a token counts outgoing volume or transfers per sender, any account can use up the allowance of the PoolManager in every period, and each later take of that token reverts (src/types/Currency.sol:82-86). That would freeze withdrawals from every pool of the token without any issuer action. Earlier work looked at zero amount transfers (lead L-208) and at one USDG setting on Robinhood Chain. No unit combined a per sender limit with the free loan.

attempts.answer: Monad part. No pooled token of size limits what one address may send or hold over a period. For all 8,375 tokens with a balance the PoolManager address sent its whole balance out and received it back four times in one simulated call. 8,310 complete all rounds, including the 45 tokens with the largest reserves, and 22 single pool tokens ran out of gas in simulation. The 38 tokens that reject a transfer do so on the first attempt because of creator gates or the Curvance pause, which is no quota. The wrapped stock tokens were read from source: the transfer hook tests pause and the sanctions list only. A third party deposit into a Curvance market for the PoolManager does not start a hold period for it. The network level part is covered by the cycle 1 clearance that the reserve balance rule skips accounts with contract code. MegaETH is not named in the lead. Its 67 tokens pass the same test, and its block budget for new state is F-042.

leads.question: For each guard and each accounting statement in the custody path (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114 and 279-378, src/types/Currency.sol:40-96, src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57, src/ERC6909.sol:25-48, src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-175 and the four transient slot libraries), which test in test/ would fail if the line were removed, inverted or moved to the other branch? List the lines that no test and no NatSpec sentence pins. For each of them, name the network feature that decides whether the unpinned behaviour is safe: a native face, an enshrined token, a currency without code or at a precompile, a batch or bundle transaction.
leads.why: Cycle 3 showed that the source satisfies every test and comment. It did not show which behaviour the tests never exercise. The tests run on a plain EVM with ordinary tokens and one model of a native face (src/test/NativeERC20.sol), so a weakness that needs a network feature to matter would sit where no test looks. Two such places are known and were judged harmless: the success of a transfer to a currency without code (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74) and the collection of native fees while a native face is synced (src/ProtocolFees.sol:49-52). A full list tells the network units which lines to aim at. The check uses only files of this repository and needs no compiler.

leads.question: In the Jenner release of bnb-chain/bsc, which is public before activation on 2026-12-08: which entry points of the CAS20 native code and of the other stateful precompiles can an account without a role call, can any of them change the balance of another holder, can transfer return success with empty data or true without lowering the caller's balance by the amount, what does balanceOf return for an address that holds native BNB, and does any of this code call a contract with caller 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe or with a value it takes from no balance?
leads.why: The PoolManager accepts empty return data or true as a successful transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74) and credits native value from msg.value alone (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354). BNB Smart Chain is the one network where a frame from the system address carries value that nobody paid. The leads L-029 and L-124 wait for activation, and the sweep of the CAS20 address range describes addresses that have no code until then. Reading the source now leaves time to act before pools hold CAS20 tokens.

leads.question: Call web3_clientVersion twenty times on each of the 21 endpoints in state/networks.json. Which endpoints answer from more than one client family or version? For each such chain, which client does the block producer run, and which cleared items of cycles 1 to 3 cite a source that belongs to the other client?
leads.why: The Celo endpoint answered from a reth based client eight times and from a Geth build four times, and two clearances of cycle 3 each read one of the two. Every item worded as the endpoint reports X assumes one client. A probe through eth_call describes whichever node answered, and a source reading describes whichever repository the unit picked. The OP Mainnet endpoint reports a development build and the Polygon endpoint a private patch, so the same doubt may apply there.

leads.question: Settle F-024 with one observation. Read crates/builder/src/flashblocks/context.rs and crates/rcs-filter/src/config.rs of okx/xlayer-reth for what the per transaction observation limits count (the default is 10,000 native transfers, 10,000 event bindings and 10,000 call frame observations). Then look for an X Layer transaction mined after 10 November 2026 that exceeds one of those limits. Does one exist?
leads.why: With the filter enabled the builder denies every transaction whose capture exceeds a limit, and denies every transaction of a block that has no pinned rule snapshot. One mined transaction above a limit would show that the filter is off on the sequencer. The absence of such a transaction over two weeks would be weak evidence that it is on. F-024 has been plausible for three cycles on this one fact, and L-187 came back inconclusive. If the limits count only events that match a rule, say so and close this route.

leads.question: On Tempo, walk sync, a liquidity removal and settle with the StorageCredits precompile 0x1060000000000000000000000000000000000000 as currency: by how much does balanceOf(PoolManager) rise for one removed position, and does the settle credit equal the number of cleared slots? Can the credit leave in any form other than an ERC-6909 claim? Separately, what does an add of one new position cost in gas when the PoolManager's credit balance is zero and when it is not, and can an account keep that balance at zero by creating single slot entries such as setOperator approvals?
leads.why: The precompile answers balanceOf(PoolManager) with a counter (13 at block 50,356,964) that rises inside a transaction whenever a PoolManager slot is cleared, by the text of TIP-1060. That is a ledger which actions at the PoolManager raise, the shape lead L-166 asked about, and the theme unit did not list it. The precompile rejects transfer, so the expected result is a credit that can only be minted as a claim (src/PoolManager.sol:322-329), like the EntryPoint case. The credits belong to the PoolManager account and are spent by whoever creates PoolManager storage next, which moves the 245,000 gas per slot between users (assumption A9). The answer also shows whether a later Tempo release that makes credits transferable would turn the counter into a currency.

leads.question: On Base, Zora, Unichain, Ethereum, Arbitrum One and BNB Smart Chain, which five hook addresses appear most often in the Initialize logs of the PoolManager over the last 500,000 blocks (the hook is the third data word of the log), what are their flag bits, and which of them have the return delta flags that let a hook take from the caller's delta?
leads.why: Cycle 3 made this count for Robinhood Chain, Elysium and X Layer and found that one hook serves a large share of pools. The same count is missing for the chains with the most pools. It feeds the check of what a hook does when the PoolManager calls it for a pool it did not create (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:178-335), and it sizes F-004 per chain.

leads.question: Is there an unredeemed retryable ticket on Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain or Elysium, a failed message recorded in L2CrossDomainMessenger on OP Mainnet or Base, or a failed state sync on Polygon whose execution would transfer or mint a token, or send native value, to the PoolManager address of that chain?
leads.why: Anyone can redeem a retryable ticket or replay a failed message. If one of them pays the PoolManager, any account can trigger the payment between sync and settle and book it as its own (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364), which is the mechanism of F-041 with a bridge as the source. The amount would be a third party's misdirected deposit, so the expected size is small.

leads.question: Through the HyperEVM Quoter 0x108Bfe38532C98f8Cd8D7Ab49c9dDAa3675a1c5e, what gas does a swap use per empty bitmap word and per initialized tick crossed in a pool with tick spacing 1, and how many of each fit in a block of 3,000,000 gas?
leads.why: F-039 has evidence marked inferred from repository snapshots. The Arbitrum unit measured 6,837,251 gas for a sweep over 2,677 bitmap words on Arbitrum One, about 2,550 gas per word, with the same Quoter method. One measurement on HyperEVM replaces the inferred figure and bounds how cheaply an account can place dust ticks that push another user's swap past a small block (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344-430).

leads.question: What do the functions of ReservesLens at 0x0000001b173C3bbF3984D417d8614E3eed34865B do (14,142 bytes on Ethereum, with the selectors 0x50183386, 0x5333569f, 0x6df8f9b8, 0x8fe532cc, 0x9169ac83, 0xe4811f2e and 0xf95138f2)? Does any of them call sync, unlock, take or settle on the PoolManager, hold token approvals, or expose a callback that another account can reach?
leads.why: The deployments page lists this contract at one address on all 21 networks, and it is the one listed contract that no unit has read. A lens that calls sync changes the synced currency for the rest of the transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), and a lens that opens an unlock is one more caller of the custody functions. The expected result is a read only helper.

leads.question: What are the verified sources, or failing that the decompiled dispatch tables, of ELO on Elysium and of the wrapper tokens v4MSTR and v4CRCL on X Layer? For ELO: in which slot does the transfer budget live, who besides the address returned by hook() can write it, and is it cleared at the end of the hook call or only at the end of the transaction? For the wrappers: who can change allowedWrappers and the recipient allow list?
leads.why: The finding on these tokens rests on selector names from a public signature database and on read only calls. ELO keeps its budget in transient storage, so a budget left open after the hook returns could be used by any later caller in the same transaction, for example in a bundle, to move ELO into or out of the PoolManager (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). This settles the open part of the finding and decides whether its actor stays pool-creator.

leads.question: In which order does the MegaETH sequencer take pending transactions, and does a transaction that was skipped for a block level limit keep its place ahead of later arrivals? Ask the operator, or watch the mini-block stream while two accounts send marked transactions in a known order.
leads.why: Blocks are not sorted by priority fee. Under arrival order a queue of state filling transactions delays everyone by its length, which is what F-042 now assumes. Measuring it needs sent transactions, which this review does not do.

leads.question: Does the wrapped stock token implementation at 0x76c6851ea0b2741eedcbbed240715e8817e85583 compile from WrappedBackedTokenImplementation.sol of the Backed repository? Its 46 selectors match. The bytecode was not compared because no compiler is installed, and the contract is not verified on Sourcify.

leads.question: Read the shMON implementation (120,874 bytes, source in FastLane-Labs/fastlane-contracts) for functions through which an account other than the holder changes a holder's plain balance, such as agent transfers and zero yield tranche conversions.

leads.question: Classify the hooks of the Monad pools. 2,774 hook addresses appear in Initialize logs, 4,726 pools use 0x94f802a9efe4dd542fdbd77a25d9e69a6dc828cc and 900 use 0x580ca49389d83b019d07e17e99454f2f218e2dc0. Which of them hold PoolManager claims or can change fees or block removals for pools with pooled value?

leads.question: For the 20 tokens with the largest value at the Monad PoolManager outside the wrapped stock set (USDC, GHO, cbBTC, syrupUSDC, AUSD, mUSD, bridged WETH, WBTC, apxUSD, USDT0, shMON and the next ones), does the transfer path in the verified source or the bytecode contain a per sender volume, count or time rule of any size?

A quota in absolute units above four times the PoolManager balance, or a rule counted per day, passes that test, and a caller can repeat take and settle hundreds of times per transaction at no cost (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). leads.question: When one currency of a pool rejects transfers from the PoolManager, can a position held through the deployed PositionManager on Monad (0x5b7ec4a94ff9bedb700fb82ab09d5846972f4016) still be closed, by minting ERC-6909 claims for the blocked currency or by clearing its delta, so that the other currency is paid out?

leads.question: Does HyperCore check an AQAv2 treasury designation against the named address, for example refuse an address with code or one that holds none of the token, and can the treasury deployer change the address after activation without a new validator vote?
